title: Only Two Species Make Hooks. Humans and This Bird

scenes.text: Only two species on Earth are known to make hooks. We're one. The other is a bird.
It's the New Caledonian crow, from an island in the South Pacific.
It snaps a twig, trims it, and shapes one end into a hook.
Researchers at St Andrews found wild crows use hooked tools the right way round, even when handed them upside down.
Scientists still can't say whether the crows understand how the tools work.
So next time someone says bird brain, remember the hook.

description:
Only humans and New Caledonian crows are known to make hooks in nature.
St Andrews researchers found wild crows use hooked tools the right way round, even when handed them upside down.
